SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY.
D
S. 2, Special Branch,
March 22, 1935.

Memorandum on A.J. Gartman (Hardman), Soviet
journalist.

Abraham Joseph Gartman alias Hardman arrived in
Shanghai from Tientsin on December 4, 1933 together with
his wife, Mrs. Cecilia Gartman, and has since been residing
in this city. He is a Soviet citizen, who was born on
September 8, 1899 at Gomel, Russia, and is a journalist
by profession.

In Shanghai Gartman works as a correspondent of
the Soviet newspaper PRAVDA, official organ of the Russian
Communist Party, and the Moscow Committee of the Party.

Following their arrival here they put up at the
Embassy Hotel. Mr. Gartman then left for Nanking where,
it is reported, a reception was given in his honour by
Mr. Li Ti Tsing, Director of the Publicity Bureau of the
Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Upon his return to Shanghai
on December 10 they went to live at Apartment 519 Embankment
Building, their present address.

A.Hardman, Soviet citizen, reported to be a corres-
pondent of a Moscow newspaper, arrived in Shanghai from Tientsin
on December 4, 1933. He stayed at the Embassy Hotel until Decem-
ber 7, when he left for Nanking by rail. Mrs Hardman, his wife, who
arrived together with him is still staying at the Embassy Hotel,
Room No 23.
